sub_scenario.family: APAC verbal ownership under incomplete records
sub_scenario.one_line: semiconductor yield engineer: avoid assigning a cause from uncalibrated measurements

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the semiconductor yield engineer and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The fab yield log review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can read a completed wafer count from the yield log.
Does that explain a yield drop?
No, counts do not determine cause.
Someone new shadowed me in the APAC bridge this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the wafer-disposition handoff into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For an abrupt yield decline, I write a provenance sheet separating tool readings, operator observations, and uncalibrated metrology results.
Why preserve provenance?
So the receiving engineer can judge what supports a disposition.
I can request a metrology rerun.
Does a rerun itself identify the defect?
No, it only obtains another measurement.
I archived last cycle's notes on the fab yield log and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The 06:30 Taipei bridge occurs before the lot reaches the next lithography stage at 07:05.
Can disposition be reconsidered later?
Not before the lot advances.
A vendor call about the semiconductor yield engineer ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the APAC bridge checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the wafer-disposition handoff.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the fab yield log records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I once verbally blamed a coating tool from an operator remark and held three lots; calibration later showed the metrology baseline had drifted.
What was the impact?
Good lots missed their processing window.
I sketched next week's plan for the wafer-disposition handoff before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the semiconductor yield engineer updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The fab lobby is displaying a new safety poster.
Does the poster bear on the yield cause?
No, it is only workplace context.
I compared two options for the fab yield log tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the APAC bridge handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How will I respond to a request for verbal wafer-disposition ownership on the Taipei bridge?
